title: Finite degree is invariant under close analytic embeddings
statement: Let $F,H$ be complete fields with nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values [def-weil-field], and let $\alpha,\beta:F\to H$ be isometric field embeddings. Suppose $0<c<1$ and $|\alpha(a)-\beta(a)|\le c|a|$ for every $a\in F$. If $H/\alpha(F)$ is finite, then $H/\beta(F)$ is finite and $$[H:\alpha(F)]=[H:\beta(F)].$$ The images here are subfields of $H$; the degrees are their vector-space dimensions.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.3, printed p. 48; the weak bound by c specializes its strict bound using any c<c′<1, and zero is excluded from the strict inequality.

proof.text: Put $A=\alpha(F)$ and $B=\beta(F)$, and $n=[H:A]$. The map $F\to A$ is an isometric field isomorphism, so $A$ is complete: pull a Cauchy sequence back to $F$, take its limit there, and apply $\alpha$. It has a nontrivial absolute value because $F$ does. Choose $r=(1+c)/2$, so $c<r<1$, and apply [lem-trf-finite-ultrametric-almost-orthogonal-basis] to $H$ as an $A$-vector space with norm $|\cdot|_H$. Multiplicativity gives homogeneity and the nonarchimedean inequality gives the ultrametric axiom. Obtain an $A$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ with $r\max_i |a_i||e_i|\le|\sum_i\alpha(a_i)e_i|$ for every $a_i\in F$. Since $H$ is a field, $n\ge1$.

source.place: Temkin, Lemma 6.3.3, printed p. 48; explicit weak-bound version and assembly written by Q36, with the local source copy requested in report.md.

proof.text: For $x\in H$, write its unique expansion $x=\sum_i\alpha(a_i)e_i$, and define $P(x)=\sum_i\beta(a_i)e_i\in W:=\sum_i B e_i$. Iterating $|u+v|\le\max(|u|,|v|)$ over this finite sum and using multiplicativity gives $$|x-P(x)|\le\max_i |\alpha(a_i)-\beta(a_i)||e_i|\le c\max_i |a_i||e_i|\le(c/r)|x|.$$ Put $q=c/r$, so $0<q<1$. In particular this estimate includes $x=0$, whose coefficients and image under $P$ are zero. No linearity of $P$ over $A$ or $B$ is asserted.

source.place: Temkin, Lemma 6.3.3, printed p. 48; explicit weak-bound version and assembly written by Q36, with the local source copy requested in report.md.

proof.text: The map $F\to B$ is also an isometric field isomorphism, so the same Cauchy-sequence argument makes $B$ complete and its norm nontrivial. Regard $H$ as a Hausdorff topological $B$-vector space using its metric and multiplication in $H$, and $W$ as a subspace with the subspace topology. It is finite-dimensional because $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ span it. Thus [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-subspace-closed] says $W$ is closed in $H$; this uses only finite-dimensionality of $W$, not of $H/B$. For arbitrary $x\in H$ set $s_0=0$ and $s_{m+1}=s_m+P(x-s_m)$. Inductively $s_m\in W$, and the estimate of step 2 gives $|x-s_{m+1}|\le q|x-s_m|$, hence $|x-s_m|\le q^m|x|$. Since $0<q<1$, the right side tends to zero, so $s_m\to x$. Closedness gives $x\in W$. Consequently $W=H$, and $H/B$ is finite.

source.place: Temkin, Lemma 6.3.3, printed p. 48; explicit weak-bound version and assembly written by Q36, with the local source copy requested in report.md.

proof.text: To check independence, suppose $\sum_i\beta(a_i)e_i=0$, and put $M=\max_i|a_i||e_i|$ and $z=\sum_i\alpha(a_i)e_i$. Step 1 gives $rM\le|z|$, while the same finite-sum bound as in step 2 gives $|z|\le cM$. Since $r>c$ and $M\ge0$, this forces $M=0$. Each $e_i$ is nonzero, so $|a_i|=0$ for every $i$, and therefore every $a_i=0$. All $B$-coefficients arise uniquely as $\beta(a_i)$, proving independence over $B$. Together with step 3 this makes the $e_i$ a $B$-basis of $H$. By [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], its $n$ elements give $[H:B]=n=[H:A]$.
